newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM radiation hearing adjourned to July 3.
newsitem.headline: KLM radiation hearing adjourned to July 3.

text.p: The Dutch transport ministry said on Tuesday a closed hearing into the exposure of passengers to radiation on a London-bound KLM flight last month had been adjourned until July 3.
"It transpired during the first round of talks that a subsequent round will be necessary because not all issues could be raised," the ministry said in a statement.
KLM was not immediately available for comment.
The ministry said the inquiry would hear evidence from six KLM representatives, including cargo chief Jacques Ancher.
The case arose from a shipment of slightly radioactive medical equipment on KLM's KL129 passenger flight from Amsterdam to London on May 2.

Routine checks on arrival by British inspectors showed the shipment, sent by Mallinckrodt, a Dutch firm of medical equipment suppliers, emitted higher levels of radiation than indicated in freight documents.
KLM is alleged to have neglected to carry out the required checks when accepting the cargo and to have failed to report the incident to Dutch civil aviation authorities.

"After the conclusion of investigations by the aviation inspectorate and government transport inspectorate and based on the information given by KLM and Mallinckrodt, (the ministry) will decide whether to act on its intention to conditionally withdraw the permits held by both companies for the transport of hazardous materials," the government statement said.
